messages.author: 2b4c5841aca584ce
messages.subject: Post-stratify and Multiplier
parts:
Dear all,

There are two things I would like to do in R and I'm wondering if "Distance libraries" can do that.
I already know how to do that in the distance software but I would like to be able to run all my analysis with R.

The first thing is including post-stratification when estimate the density (and abundance). I use the following characteristics in the "estimate" tab in the "model   definition" window of the Distance software:
Post-stratify using:
Layer type: Sample
Field name: Year
Sample def: Sample
Quantities to estimate and level of resolution:
Global(Density, Encounter rate and Cluster size)
Stratum(Density and Encounter rate)
Global density estimate: Mean (weighted by Total effort in stratum)
 
I want to calculate annual abundance using the detection function and cluster size both fitted over all years.

Can I do the same in R?

The other question is if I can apply a multiplier also in R (I do that in Distance using the Multipliers tab of the model definition window)

Any advice is welcome.
Thank you!

messages.author: 350dad0a615d36db
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Post-stratify and Multiplier
parts:
Dear Camilo, listfolk,

To your first question, at present mrds/Distance doesn't offer this kind
of post-stratification, though it is something I am actively working on
at the moment. An example of the kind of stratification currently
offered in mrds (via it's simpler Distance package interface) is
available at http://distancesampling.org/R/vignettes/minke.html

To your second question, multipliers are possible by modifying the
effort attached to each transect. For information on setting up your
data, you may want to look at the ?flatfile manual page in the Distance
package for how to set up your data.


Hope this helps!

best,
--dave
